subject: Uptime calculation dispute — edge outage + maintenance overlap
messages:
From: Helios Analytics <ops@helios-analytics.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform availability - request for SLA re-calculation

Hi Sean,

Thanks for following up. We reviewed the uptime statement you provided and the credit calculation — Helios still disagrees with the final tally. Our operations team measured sustained request failures and elevated latency from 2026-07-29T22:05:00Z to 2026-07-30T02:40:00Z (approximately 4h35m) that materially impacted customer-facing features. Your report marks part of that window as "scheduled maintenance" and excludes it from the SLA calculation; however:

- The maintenance notification we received (copy attached) was sent to billing@helios-analytics.com, not to ops@ or the alerts distribution. We therefore did not treat this as planned downtime.
- During the affected window, we observed both a CDN edge fault (third-party) and falling back to your regional secondary routing — which still returned 503s for a prolonged period.

We are asking Redwood to:
1) Share the raw uptime computation and what intervals were excluded/why.
2) Recalculate the monthly uptime for July with full transparency.
3) Consider this a partial degradation incident that should not be fully exempted due to the notification routing failure.

Attached: Helios timeline (xlsx) with sample request traces. Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

Best,
Aiden Park
Head of Platform, Helios Analytics

-----
Attachment: helios-incident-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet of client-observed traces and timestamps)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Helios Analytics <ops@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform availability - request for SLA re-calculation

Hi Aiden — thanks, and sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Marissa from Customer Success and Rishi on the commercial side so we can get you a clear answer and proposed remediation.

We’ll pull the server-side availability slices and the notification metadata that explain which intervals were counted as scheduled maintenance. I’ll aim to get an initial reply within 48 hours and propose a 1:1 technical review session if that would be useful.

Quick asks from our side to speed this up:
- Can you confirm the exact alert distribution you expected to receive notifications at (ops@ vs billing@)?
- Any direct examples of requests still failing after fallback began (we want a sample trace to match with our logs).

Thanks — Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Helios Analytics <ops@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform availability - request for SLA re-calculation

Hi Aiden — I pulled the incident notes and the preliminary availability calculation. Summary below, followed by our proposed remediation and credit offer.

Summary of findings:
- 2026-07-29T21:50:00Z — Redwood scheduled network maintenance (edge routing config) for 22:00Z–00:00Z for a subset of customers in us-west. Notification sent 2026-07-27T13:07:00Z to billing@helios-analytics.com (we’ll attach headers).
- 2026-07-29T22:03:00Z — Third-party CDN reported degraded edge performance globally; our edge routing attempted automated failover to the secondary region.
- 2026-07-29T22:05:00Z–2026-07-29T23:58:00Z — majority of client requests experienced increased latency and intermittent 5xxs. This overlaps both the maintenance window and the CDN outage.
- 2026-07-29T23:58:00Z–2026-07-30T02:40:00Z — partial degradation continued while we escalated to vendor support; traffic partially recovered by 02:40Z.

How we calculated uptime:
- Per our SLA, scheduled maintenance windows (announced at least 48 hours prior and under 4 hours) are excluded from uptime calculations.
- In this case the maintenance notification met our policy timing but was sent to the billing address on file. We agree that if the notification did not reach the correct on-call distribution we need to treat that as a process failure on our side.
- For the CDN outage periods that are clearly attributable to the third-party (their incident timeline matches), our standard practice has been to exclude pure third-party outages when systems can demonstrably fail over within the SLO definition. Where the vendor outage prevents failover or we failed to route traffic correctly, that portion is not excluded.

Proposed next steps / remediation:
1) We will re-run the availability calc removing the maintenance exclusion for Helios (given notification routing mismatch).
2) We will isolate what portion of the window is attributable solely to the CDN vendor vs where our routing/fallbacks failed.
3) Offer: provisional credit of 7.5% of July invoice while we complete the detailed audit (final credit subject to findings). This is above our standard auto-credit and intended as a goodwill gesture.
4) Technical commitments: change notification routing to include ops@ for Helios, and provision a dedicated fallback route within 2 weeks to reduce single-CDN dependency.

We’ll attach the raw epoched logs and the draft postmortem once the vendor provides their final timeline. If you want a tech call I can schedule it tomorrow.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment: redwood-incident-draft-postmortem.pdf

From: Helios Analytics <ops@helios-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform availability - request for SLA re-calculation

Marissa — thanks for the analysis and the provisional credit offer. We appreciate the gesture but remain concerned about two points:

1) The total affected time from our traces is larger because several of our customers continued to see elevated error rates after 02:40Z (we have traces extending to 03:20Z). We’d like the re-run to include our client traces to ensure the metrics match.
2) Even if notification went to billing@, the essence of our ask is that Redwood’s operational controls should prevent a single routing change from amplifying a vendor outage. We believe a larger credit is warranted because the combined effect took down multiple critical features.

We are open to the call and to working through the exact matching of spans, but please consider a stronger commercial remedy given downstream customer impact.

Regards,
Aiden Park
Head of Platform, Helios Analytics

-----
Attachment: helios-extended-traces.xlsx

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Helios Analytics <ops@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-04T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform availability - request for SLA re-calculation

Aiden — thank you for the patience and for sharing the additional traces. We’ve completed the expedited re-calculation and vendor correlation:

- Re-run outcome: removing the maintenance exclusion increases the total unavailability window for Helios in July to ~4h12m, which equates to a July uptime of 99.56% for your account (down from 99.84% when the maintenance exclusion was applied).
- Root cause summary: majority is attributable to the CDN edge outage (third-party) from 22:03Z–00:10Z. However, from 00:10Z–02:40Z the primary contributor was our routing configuration that failed to route a segment of traffic to the healthy pool.

Final commercial resolution we can commit to today: a one-time invoice credit of 7.5% for July plus a goodwill operational credit (50% discount on overage rates for the next billing cycle). We can increase the credit to 10% if Helios signs a 12-month reserved routing commitment (reduces our remedial cost).

Operational commitments already in motion:
- Add ops@helios-analytics.com to all maintenance notifications and verify alert routing within 24 hours.
- Deploy the dedicated fallback routing within 14 days and run a scheduled failover test.
- Deliver a finalized postmortem within 7 business days with vendor attachments.

If that package is acceptable, I’ll have Rishi prepare the credit note and Marissa will schedule the technical review. We can also schedule a leadership call if you prefer.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
